units.source_text: 源氏内大臣派几个亲信人员，偷偷地赴明石浦迎接明石姬。

en.t: Genji, the Inner Minister, sent several trusted attendants in secret to Akashi Bay to bring Lady Akashi back.

units.source_text: 明石姬这回已无可推托，只得下决心动身。

en.t: This time Lady Akashi had no way to refuse, and could only resolve to set out.

units.source_text: 但要离开这多年住惯的浦滨，又觉依依不舍，想起了父亲今后将凄凉寂寞地独居浦上，更觉心绪烦乱，悲伤不已。

en.t: Yet when she had to leave the shore where she had lived for so many years, she felt deeply reluctant to part from it; and when she thought of her father living alone there from now on in bleak loneliness, her heart grew still more troubled and her sorrow would not end.

units.source_text: 她自怜此身何以如此多愁多恨，却羡慕那些未曾接受过源氏爱情的人。

en.t: She pitied herself, wondering why her life had to be filled with so much grief and resentment, and instead envied those who had never received Genji's love.

units.source_text: 她的父母呢，近年来日夜盼望源氏内大臣迎接女儿入京，今已如愿以偿，自然欢喜无量。

en.t: As for her parents, for years they had longed day and night for Genji, the Inner Minister, to bring their daughter to the capital, and now that their wish had come true, their joy was naturally boundless.

units.source_text: 但念夫人随女儿入京，今后老夫妇不得相见，则又悲痛难堪。

en.t: But when they thought that the lady would go to the capital with their daughter and that the old couple would no longer be able to see each other, their grief became almost unbearable.

units.source_text: 明石道人日夜茫然若失，嘴里反反复复地说同一句话：“那么我以后不能再见这小宝贝了么？”

en.t: The Akashi monk was dazed day and night, as though he had lost his soul, and over and over he repeated the same words: “Then will I never see this little treasure again?”
Apart from that, he had nothing else to say.

units.source_text: 夫人也很悲伤，她想：“我俩都出家修行，多年来不曾同室而居。

en.t: The lady was also deeply saddened, and thought: “Both of us have taken religious vows and practiced the Way, and for many years we have not lived in the same room.

units.source_text: 今后教他独留浦上，有谁照顾他呢？

en.t: If he is left alone on this shore from now on, who will look after him?

units.source_text: 即使是邂逅相逢、暂叙露情之人，但在‘彼此已熟识’之后忽然离别，也不免伤心；何况我俩是正式夫妇。

en.t: Even people who meet by chance and share only a brief affection cannot help feeling sorrow if they suddenly part after coming to know each other; how much more so for us, who are formally husband and wife.

units.source_text: 我夫虽然禀性顽强，难于亲近，但这又作别论。

en.t: My husband may be stubborn by nature and hard to approach, but that is a separate matter.

units.source_text: 既已结缡，选定此浦为终老之地，总想在‘修短不可知’的存命期间共享余年。

en.t: Since we became husband and wife and chose this shore as the place where we would grow old, I always wished that, for as long as our uncertain lives might last, we would share our remaining years together.

units.source_text: 如今忽然分手，怎不教人肠断？”

en.t: Now that we must suddenly part, how could it not break my heart?”

units.source_text: 那些青年侍女，住在这乡间常嫌寂寞，现在即将迁居京都，大家欢天喜地。

en.t: The young waiting women, who had often found life in this countryside lonely, were all overjoyed now that they were about to move to Kyoto.

units.source_text: 但念今后不能再见这海边美景，又觉依依难舍，看看那去而复返的波浪，不觉泪沾襟袖。

en.t: But when they thought that they would no longer see the beauty of this seashore, they again found it hard to leave; and as they gazed at the waves coming and going, their tears, before they knew it, soaked their collars and sleeves.
